1 2.
The petitioner is arrayed as A3 in FIR No.9 of 2025 dated 01.04.2025 registered by the 1st respondent Police for the offences under Sections 419, 465, 467, 468, 471, 420 IPC.

It appears that there are civil proceedings pending between the petitioner and the de-facto complainant, and the subject matter of the dispute, including the alleged forgery, is also the subject of the said civil suit.
Subsequently, an FIR has been filed in relation to the same issue against the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.

3. Heard both sides and perused the materials available on record.
4.
This Court is of the view that the petitioner claims to have purchased the property in the year 1995 on the basis of a sale deed said to have been executed on proper stamp duty.
However, it now appears that the person who executed the Power of Attorney was an impersonator.
The de- facto complainant has also purchased the property from the original owner.

5. Such being the position, at the most, even if the petitioner had https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (
Uploaded on: 10/10/2025 05:14:41 pm ) transferred the property to some third party, the question involved is only one of title.
Since a civil suit is already pending before the competent Court to decide the ownership dispute between the parties, the matter primarily falls within the realm of civil adjudication.
6. Nevertheless, the investigation may proceed in accordance with law.

However, taking note of the fact that the dispute appears to be essentially civil in nature, and the petitioner also appears to be a victim of the alleged fraud, there shall not be any coercive steps taken against the petitioner.
The investigation shall proceed and be completed as against the other accused, and if necessary, the petitioner may be treated as a witness in the case.
7. With the above direction, the petition stands disposed of.
However, there shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
